# Explicit discovery and CLI recovery — Issue #253

This is an informed, bounded tooling study, not a zero-prior authoring benchmark.
The desired source programs are three already frozen #100 projects; their
original bytes/identities and actual binding rejections are reused unchanged.
No new external corpus source, analysis suite, source semantics, proof or
Guardian interpretation is introduced.

`first-inputs.json` and the two before snapshots preserve the initial production
CLI. The separate selected-source usage was discovered during comparison;
`additional-before.json` and `source-plan-options.rs.before.txt` preserve its
unchanged prior bytes before that repair. `baseline/`, `after-repair/` and
`after-usage-repair/` retain 18 actual invocations each, exact output and native
logs. The intermediate comparison failed because sized/selected usage lacked
the discovery path (indices 10, 13, 14). That real observation is preserved in
`first-comparison-failure.json`; it is an extracted report, not a raw subprocess
transcript. The intermediate output is not overwritten.

The final 18 pairs have zero native calls. Only three exact text-help requests
become successful; all other exit statuses remain the same. All three explicit
binding source failures retain byte-identical stdout/stderr. Main, selected,
sized, interop and JSON usage routes point to `qleisli help ecosystem`. Its
output equals the single canonical Reference chapter byte-for-byte, embedded
at compile time, with no runtime file/project/kernel/network dependency.
Extra flags and unknown topics/tools stay usage failures. JSON gains no new
success command, schema or analysis result. The later #232 topology is not chosen.

## All ten original criteria

| Criterion | Final contract and implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Distinct inferable/discoverable categories | Discovery chapter opening and Four recovery categories. |
| Classify ecosystem including QLT/QDB/QCP | Language and ecosystem map; native introduction states roles and later availability. |
| Semantic role, not spelling | Category definitions, map and naming review explicitly reject superficial similarity as a contract. |
| Deterministic correction | Correction table, named binding diagnostics, every shared usage route and actual unchanged source failures. |
| Discovery without known native names | Ordinary `--help`/`help` names the roles and leads to embedded `help ecosystem`, without requiring a project or checker. |
| Ordinary stdlib source fallback | Signature → checked source → calls → language/primitive rules, with actual incomplete migration status. |
| Sealed/external authority distinct | Specification-only category, primitive/artifact rows and rejection of reconstructed authority. |
| No misleading pseudo-analogue | Naming/review rule and six concrete safe-recovery versus false-friend examples. |
| Reference/diagnostic/stdlib cross-links | SUMMARY, authority, architecture, contributor build guide and primitive/stdlib chapter link the canonical page; CLI usage exposes it. |
| Future additions declare category | Naming and future design review explicitly require category, role, correction/discovery path and availability. |

Full diagnostic pedagogy, later syntax and tooling implementation remain their
own original Issues. This completion does not advertise those as implemented
or measure whether an unfamiliar model learned the system.

## Actual bounded validation

`latest/` and `msrv/` each pass 12 Rust CLI integration tests (three new and nine
existing selected-source tests), plus 12 independently decoded JSON CLI tests.
Python discovers 14 tests and skips two Linux-only filesystem cases on macOS;
their reasons remain in the test source and actual `skipped=2` output. Both
actual Rust 1.98.1/1.85.0 runs pass all-target Clippy and formatting and bind the
same 105 source/test inputs with identical before/after hashes. No ignored or
maximum stress test is selected. `cli-build*` retain both actual build records.

The current inventory changes only three reviewed CLI hashes, and coverage
changes its dependent source binding. Public markers, authority, proof/cutover
gates and boundary obligations remain identical; before files and the exact
repair patch preserve that review. Help precedes execution only for the three
exact supported argument vectors; invalid requests cannot suppress a check or
claim acceptance. No native definition or admitted guarantee changes.

`policies/` passes source docs, pinned mdBook 0.5.4 build, rendered HTML/print
links, inventory/coverage, 14 coverage policy regressions, authoring integrity
and constitutional continuity against 7cc6b5f. This is no local Lean replay,
full CI or release certificate. `files.json` freezes the final packet and
reviewed inputs; GitHub remains the work/decision ledger.
